summary_en: Nittoc Construction acquired all issued shares of Chiken Techno Co., Ltd. for a strategic expansion of its foundation and ground improvement business. The acquisition, executed through a share purchase agreement on September 28, 2026, combines Nittoc's nationwide infrastructure and expertise with Chiken Techno's customer base and specialized capabilities in residential and low-rise building foundation work.
title_en: Notice Regarding Acquisition of Shares of Chiken Techno Co., Ltd. (Full Subsidiary Status)
translation_en_brief:
On September 28, 2026, Nittoc Construction executed a share purchase agreement to acquire all 200 issued shares of Chiken Techno Co., Ltd., representing 100% ownership. Prior to the share acquisition, Chiken Techno will undergo organizational restructuring including a merger and business separation. The acquisition is positioned as strategic growth investment aligned with Nittoc's medium-term management plan (2026–2028) and long-term vision targeting 150 billion yen in sales and 12 billion yen in operating profit by fiscal 2036.

Chiken Techno, based in Sagamihara, Kanagawa, specializes in foundation surveys, design, and ground improvement works for residential and low-rise buildings across the Tokyo and Kanagawa regions. It maintains established relationships with regional house builders and general contractors and operates a vertically integrated system from survey and design through construction and warranty coordination. The company possesses specialized expertise including WINPILE construction methodology and operational capabilities for high-turnover small projects.

Nittoc views the acquisition as combining its nationwide infrastructure, technical expertise, and management foundation in the foundation and ground improvement sector with Chiken Techno's residential market access and specialized construction capabilities. Post-acquisition strategy includes strengthening construction capacity and human resources through recruitment, training, and know-how sharing; gradual business expansion into new territories leveraging Nittoc's regional facilities and equipment; and enhanced safety, quality, and management governance. The acquisition is part of Nittoc's three-year capital allocation plan allocating 13 billion yen to future investment including M&A activities, while maintaining financial soundness and sustaining shareholder distributions.
